transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I came in because things at work have just been getting to me. The district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching, and I’m still managing to get through the day, but I feel wound up and discouraged in a way that doesn’t feel like me.

I’ve also started putting off lesson plans and emails—things I used to just handle without really thinking about it.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure out of things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or activities with your students?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change in enjoying things, exactly. I think I still like the things I usually like, but I may not be making as much room for them lately.
Have you found yourself losing interest in doing things, even if you still know you'd enjoy them if you did them?
I don’t think so, not in a clear way. It’s more that I get busy or tired and don’t start things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in them.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless more days than not?

I wouldn’t say hopeless, no. I do feel discouraged and kind of wound up since this new work rollout was added, and it’s not like me. But I’m still getting through my days. It’s more stress and frustration than feeling sad most days.
Have you been more irritable lately, even with people you care about, like family or students?

Yes, I think a little. Since the district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching, I’ve felt more wound up and discouraged than usual. I still get through the day, but I can tell I’m not quite myself, and I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails I used to just handle.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level lately, or been feeling unusually tired even when you haven’t done much?
Not really a big drop, no. I mean, I’m tired at the end of the day, but that feels pretty normal for teaching. I haven’t noticed being wiped out when I haven’t done much.
Have you noticed that you're getting less done than usual at work or home because of how you've been feeling?

Yes, a little. I’m still teaching and taking care of the main things I need to, but I’ve definitely been pushing back planning deadlines. And I’ve needed a few reminders from colleagues about things I normally would’ve handled on my own.
Have you felt a persistent sense of worry or tension most days over the past six months because of everything going on at work?

I wouldn’t say it’s been six months of constant worry, exactly. It’s more that since this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout got added on top of my regular teaching, I’ve felt wound up and discouraged most days. I’m still getting through work, but I don’t feel like myself, and I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails that I used to just take care of.
Have you found that you're not getting any enjoyment out of things you used to like, even when you do them?
I don’t think so. I still enjoy things when I actually do them. It might take me a little more effort to get started sometimes, but once I’m there, I can still have a good time.
Have you found yourself doing less—like speaking more slowly, moving more slowly, or just not doing as much during the day—as a result of how you've been feeling?

Not really slower in how I talk or move, but I am doing a bit less in the sense that I’m not keeping up the way I used to. I’m still teaching and handling the basics, but I’ve missed or pushed back some planning deadlines, and coworkers have had to remind me about things I’d normally get done on my own.
Looking back, would you say that most days feel harder emotionally now compared to before this work rollout started, even if you’re not feeling sad all the time?

Yes, most days do feel harder emotionally than they did before the rollout. I’m not sad all the time, but since that bilingual SEL work got added on top of everything else, I feel more wound up and discouraged. I’m still making it through the day, but I don’t feel like myself, and I’ve been putting off lesson plans and emails that I used to just handle.
Have you been having trouble relaxing, or feeling on edge or restless since this new work rollout started?

Yes, I have. Since the district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching, I feel wound up a lot more than usual. I’m still getting through the day, but I don’t relax the way I used to, and I get discouraged. It’s not like me, and I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would’ve just handled.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or having trouble calming down since this new work rollout started?

Yes. I’ve been feeling anxious and kind of wound up since the district added that bilingual SEL rollout on top of my regular teaching. I’m still getting through the day, but it’s harder to calm down, and I feel discouraged in a way that doesn’t feel like me. I’ve also been putting off lesson plans and emails that I used to just take care of.
Have you had several days in a row where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so. I’ve had rough days, definitely, but not where I was down or uninterested most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. It feels more like stress and discouragement coming and going.
Have you ever had a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
No, I don’t think I’ve ever had a stretch like that. I’ve had bad days here and there, but not two weeks where I felt down most of the day every day or stopped enjoying things like that.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or very low for several days in a row, even before this work-related stress started?
Not really. I mean, I’ve had stressful days or felt upset for a day or two, like anyone, but I can’t think of a time before this where I felt very low for several days in a row.
